payload.title: Review TASK-4730
Roost gating: INFORM addressed to an endpoint by name always wakes the LLM (L-S2 only holds for capability-addressed informs)
payload.body: GatingDispatcher.dispatch (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/roost/gating.py) returns WAKE_LLM for any unsolicited INFORM addressed by name, regardless of the registered handler. Gate L-S2 (test_gate_ls2_inform_no_reply.py, TASK-4729) therefore uses capability_filter='digest.*' with a wildcard handler instead of a by-name address. If the spec intends a by-name INFORM with a non-decision handler to be stored without waking, dispatch needs to consult handlers.resolve() on the directly_addressed path too. Verify against spec FEAT-747 L-S2 wording and decide.

payload.title: Roost endpoint never enforces hop limit, token budget or deadline at runtime (AC-5)
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/roost/endpoint.py: (1) line ~96 `self.dispatcher.dispatch(msg)` passes no hops, so ProtocolEngine.accept never exceeds hop_limit; (2) `self.engine.charge(...)` return value (a failure Transition) is discarded and `getattr(response, "tokens", 0)` is always 0 because RoostMessage has no `tokens` field; (3) ProtocolEngine.expire() has no caller anywhere in roost/, so deadlines never emit failure(TIMEOUT) — a timed-out request only raises RoostFailure locally via asyncio.wait_for; (4) a hop-failure Transition(kind='closed') goes to _resolve_pending(msg) with the ORIGINAL msg, which would complete the future successfully instead of raising HOP_LIMIT. Engine-level behaviour is tested; end-to-end is not. Fix: thread hops through dispatch, act on charge()'s transition, run expire() periodically (or per-request), resolve pending futures with the failure message. Found by the FEAT-747 code review (reproduced with a probe script).

payload.title: Roost endpoint does not propagate the caller PermissionContext and does not enforce the grant on explicit-receiver paths (AC-12/13/35)
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/roost/endpoint.py: (1) nothing under roost/ sets RoostMessage.permission_context or auth_token on outbound messages (only the codec/bridge read them), so _run_tool calls execute_tool(..., permission_context=None) for every inbound request — under PBAC every Roost call is denied, otherwise it runs unguarded. The endpoint needs a caller PermissionContext source (constructor argument or ContextVar) stamped onto outbound messages. Needs a design decision. (2) request(receiver=...) and query(receiver=...) skip find_capability and GrantPolicy; self.grant is stored but never read, so a caller without a grant can address any agent/tool directly. (3) serving side: _run_tool takes content['tool'] from the wire without checking it against the endpoint's advertised capabilities, and request() builds {'tool': ..., **args} so args['tool'] can override the capability's tool. Found by the FEAT-747 code review.

payload.title: Roost: cfp ignores scorer and never applies grant attenuation; expected_schema dropped; audit direction inverted (AC-8/14/26/27)
payload.body: (1) RoostEndpoint.cfp (endpoint.py ~341) does `del scorer`; GrantPolicy.attenuate has no caller outside grant.py, so AC-14 attenuation is never applied to the Award. (2) RoostEndpoint.query does `del expected_schema`, so no schema_error is ever produced; swarm_toolkit._ask_via_roost status_map has no schema_error/unknown_agent and never seeds hops from ctx.current_hops (related: issue:0f5ee739eca8). (3) Audit direction inverted: endpoint.py records every inbound message as 'served' and every outbound as 'received', contradicting audit.py's documented meaning (served on the serving agent, received on the caller). Found by the FEAT-747 code review.

payload.title: Roost review suggestions: eager roost imports, AgentTool wm key, shm multi-receiver unlink, bus multi-receiver + clear-text token, docs gaps
payload.body: From the FEAT-747 code review (all unfixed): (a) tools/agent.py:16 imports roost.endpoint at module level, pulling audit/blackboard/protocols/security on every parrot.tools.agent import — make it lazy/TYPE_CHECKING and import RoostFailure inside _execute_roost; registry/registry.py:45 also imports roost.directory eagerly. (b) AgentTool._execute_roost uses working-memory key roost:{agent}:{self.call_count}, which can collide across caller instances — use the conversation id. (c) SharedMemoryCarrier unlinks the segment on the first receiver's ack (wrong for multi-receiver sends) and _owned only exists in the sender's instance, so cross-process receivers never unlink; also residual B905 zip() without strict= at carriers/shm.py:52. (d) EventBusCarrier.to_event routes by receivers[0] only, silently dropping extra receivers, and copies auth_token in clear text into event metadata. (e) AC-31: docs/roost has only README/carriers/performatives; gating, directory, blackboard, protocols and the FEAT-746 boundary may lack dedicated pages. (f) nit: registry/capabilities/models.py has an empty `if TYPE_CHECKING: pass` block. (g) TASK-4720 InProcessCarrier excludes the sender from capability-filter broadcasts (unspecified).

payload.title: repl_worker restricted unpickler rejects pyarrow-backed DataFrames, crashing PandasAgent.ask()
payload.body:
What: with the worker-mode Python REPL (default `execution_mode="worker"`), every non-streaming `PandasAgent.ask()` that loads a DataFrame with pyarrow-backed columns crashes at the end of the turn with:

  _pickle.UnpicklingError: repl_worker: refusing to unpickle pyarrow.lib._restore_array (insecure-deserialization guard — module not on the allowlist)

Where: `PandasAgent.ask()` -> `_infer_data_variable_from_tools()` (bots/data.py ~L2547) -> `PythonREPLTool.get_var()` -> `repl_worker/handle.py get_var` -> `protocol.decode_value` -> `_safe_pickle_loads`. `_SAFE_PICKLE_TOP_LEVEL_MODULES` = {pandas, numpy, datetime, decimal, collections, builtins, pathlib}; a DataFrame with ArrowDtype / pyarrow string columns pickles through `pyarrow.lib._restore_array`, so `find_class` refuses it.

Repro (2026-10-26): agents/pokemon_finance.py (DatasetManager query slug `pokemon_projections_exec_detail` + pg table sources), ENV=prod, `await agent.ask(question="which row line has the highest contribution to revenue")` -> 3/3 runs crashed after the tool loop finished. `ask_stream()` on the same question succeeds (it does not go through `_infer_data_variable_from_tools`). Scheduled jobs calling `ask()` (e.g. a daily report) are affected too.

Why it matters: the answer is computed and then lost; any PandasAgent whose sources yield pyarrow dtypes is unusable through `ask()` in worker mode. Current workaround: `python_repl_execution_mode = "inprocess"` on the agent (loses process isolation), as agents/finance_reporter.py does.

Suggested fix (needs a security look, it is the FEAT-380 guard): either allowlist the specific pyarrow reconstruction callables (e.g. `pyarrow.lib._restore_array`, `pyarrow.lib.type_for_alias`, ArrowDtype/ArrowExtensionArray in pandas) rather than all of `pyarrow`, or serialize DataFrames across the worker boundary via Arrow IPC / parquet bytes instead of pickle. Also, `_infer_data_variable_from_tools` should catch decode errors per variable and skip that candidate instead of failing the whole turn.

payload.reason: repl_worker value codec now carries DataFrames/Series as Arrow IPC (pickle guard unchanged; fallback casts pyarrow dtypes to object); PandasAgent inference skips a candidate whose get_var fails. FEAT-750 branch feat-FEAT-750-bots-data-fixes, b0106db53.

payload.title: SkillRegistryMixin resolves skill dirs and DB namespace from bot `name` instead of `agent_id` → load_skill "Skill not found"
payload.body:
## What
`SkillRegistryMixin` uses `getattr(self, "name", None) or getattr(self, "agent_id", "default")` as the agent id (mixin.py ~lines 251, 321, 361, 402) and `getattr(self, "name", "agent")` (~676, 742, 770). Since `name` is the bot's display name and is almost always set, `agent_id` is effectively never used. The docstring promises `AGENTS_DIR/{agent_id}/skills/`.

## Repro
Agent with `agent_id = "pokemon_finance"`, skills in `agents/pokemon_finance/skills/pnl_contract_summary/SKILL.md`, instantiated as `PokemonFinance(name="Pokemon Finance")`:
- log: `SkillFileRegistry loaded: 0 skills from .../agents/Pokemon Finance/skills`
- `load_skill(name="pnl_contract_summary")` -> `ToolResult(status="error", error="Skill not found: pnl_contract_summary")`; `list_skill_commands` -> "No skills available."
- `skills_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` also creates a stray `agents/Pokemon Finance/skills/` directory.
- The model never receives the skill body and improvises the output format; `/pnl_summary` silently degrades. The identity layer works only because it uses an explicit `identity_dir`.

## Why it matters
Any agent whose `name` differs from `agent_id` (display names with spaces/capitals) silently loses its file skills, per-tenant skill trees and its learned-skills dir; the DB `SkillRegistry` namespace becomes `{org_id}/{name}`.

## Suggested fix
Resolve one id via a single helper preferring `agent_id`, falling back to `name`. Not a pure rename: persisted DB skills (namespace `org/{name}`), learned skills and tenant trees under name-based dirs move, so add a compatibility fallback (load name-based dir/namespace when the id-based one is empty, log a deprecation) or a migration. Add a test with `name != agent_id`.

## Workaround in use
`agents/pokemon_finance.py` sets `skill_paths = [AGENT_DIR / "skills"]` (FEAT-188 path), which loads the skills regardless of `name`.

payload.title: Google client strips every streaming chunk: words glued ("thehighest") and Markdown tables collapsed, also in final text / saved history
payload.body:
## What
`GoogleGenAIClient._safe_extract_text(chunk, is_stream_chunk=True)` (client.py:2743) applies `.strip()` in three places: `response.text.strip()`, `part.text.strip()` and `"".join(text_parts).strip()`. For stream chunks this removes the whitespace/newlines at every chunk boundary, and a whitespace-only chunk (e.g. `"\n\n"`) returns `""` and is dropped. `is_stream_chunk` is only used to pick the log message.

`ask_stream` yields these stripped chunks (client.py:4429-4447) and builds the final text as `"".join(all_assistant_text)` (client.py:4562), so the returned AIMessage and the persisted conversation turn are corrupted too.

## Repro (offline)
Feed synthetic `types.GenerateContentResponse` chunks `["The row line with the", " highest contribution is **40105", "**.\n\n", "| Account | Amount |\n", "|---|---|\n", "| 40105 | $1,278,863.13 |\n"]` through `_safe_extract_text(..., is_stream_chunk=True)` and join:
- want: `'The row line with the highest contribution is **40105**.\n\n| Account | Amount |\n|---|---|\n| 40105 | $1,278,863.13 |\n'`
- got:  `'The row line with thehighest contribution is **40105**.| Account | Amount ||---|---|| 40105 | $1,278,863.13 |'`
Seen live on pokemon_finance (gemini-3.1-pro-preview, ENV=prod): "thehighest", "purerevenue".

## Suggested fix
When `is_stream_chunk=True`, return text parts verbatim (no strip, keep whitespace-only chunks; still skip thought parts and function-call-only chunks). Keep stripping for complete responses. Add a unit test with the chunk sequence above.

## Not verified
Whether other clients (OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq...) strip stream chunks the same way; whether extra newlines seen inside a table from non-streaming `ask()` share this code path.

payload.title: Tests reference removed BotManager._build_prompt_builder / _build_from_registry — 19 failures on dev
payload.body:
On origin/dev, 19 tests fail because they reference BotManager methods that no longer exist. This was confirmed on a clean origin/dev checkout on 2026-10-27, identical to the FEAT-704 branch.

- packages/ai-parrot/tests/bots/prompts/test_yaml_prompt_config.py: 16 tests (TestYAMLAddOperation, TestYAMLCombinedOperations, TestYAMLCustomizeOperation, TestYAMLPresetSelection, TestYAMLRemoveOperation) fail with `AttributeError: type object 'BotManager' has no attribute '_build_prompt_builder'`.
- packages/ai-parrot-server/tests/studio/test_tooling_integration.py: 3 tests fail. test_yaml_agent_toolkit_persist_roundtrip fails on `'BotManager' object has no attribute '_build_from_registry'`; test_dataset_manager_datasources_in_memory and test_user_override_session_isolation fail with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'list_tools'` and `assert 0 == 2`.

Why it matters: the merge/feature-tier selector picks these up as direct importers of manager.py, so every feature that touches BotManager reports them as "new red". The baseline comparison classified them as new_red=19, baseline_red=0, so the gate shows false failures (seen in FEAT-704 PR #1821 and in TASK-4480).

Suggested fix: find the commit that removed or renamed these BotManager methods, then point the tests at the current API, or restore the helpers if the removal was accidental. Also check why select_tests' baseline did not classify them as baseline red.

payload.title: repl_worker snapshot() fails entirely when one namespace variable is not on the unpickle allowlist (e.g. an altair Chart)
payload.body: Repro: in a real worker, execute "chart = altair.Chart(df).mark_line().encode(x='index', y='a')" then await handle.snapshot() -> _pickle.UnpicklingError: repl_worker: refusing to unpickle altair.vegalite.v5.api.Chart (insecure-deserialization guard - module not on the allowlist), raised by _RestrictedUnpickler.find_class (protocol.py ~L124). altair is the REPL's supported renderer, so any agent session that binds a chart loses snapshot() for the whole namespace. Keep the guard; instead skip or placeholder the non-allowlisted entries (worker-side filtering or per-variable decode) so the remaining variables still come back. Found while fixing test_e2e_data_analysis_session (PR #1820), which now avoids binding the chart.

payload.title: Roost: hop budget (AC-5) never enforced on the wire
payload.body: ProtocolEngine.accept(hops=0) (protocols.py:266) and GatingDispatcher.dispatch(hops=0) (gating.py:92) default to 0; RoostEndpoint._on_message calls dispatcher.dispatch(msg) without hops; swarm_toolkit._ask_via_roost does not seed hops from ctx.current_hops (AC-26). failure(HOP_LIMIT) is only reachable in unit tests. Fix: carry hops through the carrier envelope/ctx and pass into dispatch.

payload.title: Roost: timeouts are caller-side only; ProtocolEngine.expire() has no caller; token budget never charged
payload.body: AC-5 requires a timed-out Request to emit failure(TIMEOUT) to the requester. protocols.py:289 expire() is never called in src/, so no failure message is emitted and stale server-side conversations never close; Subscribe/Contract Net states never expire. Also endpoint.py:123 charges tokens via getattr(response, "tokens", 0) but RoostMessage has no tokens field, so failure(TOKEN_BUDGET) never triggers. Fix: add a sweeper/timer calling expire(), emit failure(TIMEOUT), and source token usage from the real LLM response.

payload.title: Roost: RoostToolkit.send(request/query) builds malformed conversations (AC-3)
payload.body: toolkit.py forwards the LLM-chosen performative to endpoint.send(), which defaults protocol to InteractionProtocol.INFORM (endpoint.py:222). A request/query is sent under the INFORM state machine with no pending future, so the caller never receives the reply. The LLM also still picks the performative via a Literal enum (pinned by test_schemas_expose_only_the_performative_enum_and_no_grant), contradicting "the LLM never emits a performative". Fix: drop send, or route request/query through endpoint.request()/query().

payload.title: Roost: inter-agent grant (AC-12) not enforced on direct sends; cfp(scorer=) ignored
payload.body: GrantPolicy.allows/filter_matches are consulted only inside find_capability; endpoint.py:62 stores self.grant but never reads it. RoostEndpoint.request(receiver=...), query(receiver=...) and RoostToolkit.send/report with an arbitrary receiver string do no grant check, so a model can address any agent by name (fail-closed requirement violated). Separately endpoint.py:369 `del scorer` ignores cfp(scorer=) (AC-8), and expected_schema is discarded at endpoint.py:324. Fix: check grant on the send path; honour the per-call scorer/schema.

payload.title: Review TASK-4735
InMemoryHandleStore.put overwrites an existing handle key regardless of owner
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/interagent/handles.py, InMemoryHandleStore.put: stores `self._items[handle.key] = handle` unconditionally. Keys are content-addressed (sha256 of bytes), so two different owners producing identical bytes collide on the same key; the later put replaces the first owner's handle (owner, grants, descriptor), so the original owner can no longer claim it and the new owner gains it. Spec/blueprint of TASK-4739 does not define put-collision semantics, so the delivery matches the task, but the gap is a cross-tenant isolation risk. Suggested fix: on an existing key with a different owner, refuse (raise HandleClaimError) or key the store by (owner, key). Also consider validating that expires_at is consistent with ttl_s.

payload.title: Review TASK-4756
FEAT-754 emits unsupported Mermaid neighbor relationship macros
payload.body: Draft spec sdd/specs/a2ui-c4-diagrams.spec.md:303-304,503 requires Rel_Neighbor and Rel_Back_Neighbor for valid hints. Mermaid's C4 lexer has Rel/BiRel/U/D/L/R/Back/Index only (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/develop/packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/c4/parser/c4Diagram.jison lines 131-145). Exports with these hints will fail in Mermaid despite internal codec round trips passing. Remove unsupported hints or define a supported explicit fallback; validate emitted examples against upstream Mermaid.

payload.title: FEAT-754 boundary graphics lack graph viewport and roam transform
payload.body: Draft spec sdd/specs/a2ui-c4-diagrams.spec.md:664 emits raw layout-coordinate boundary frames as option.graphic while keeping existing graph layout:none and roam:true. Installed ECharts graph/createView.js maps node bounds into viewport and GraphView.js applies transform to its mainGroup, not standalone graphic elements. Frames misalign initially and detach during pan/zoom/resize. Specify shared transforms or pixel conversion with lifecycle updates, include actual render/resize/roam coverage.

payload.title: FEAT-754 round-trip guarantee excludes required normalization and semantic losses

payload.title: sdd-coder MCP server exits silently: LLM-seat children inherit the JSON-RPC stdin socket
payload.body:
## Symptom

`parrot-sdd-coder` disconnects mid-run: `Error: Connection closed` on an in-flight `coder_wait`, then `No such tool available ... has disconnected`. The reconnected server reports `job_not_found`; the job journal stays `state: "running"` and the orchestrator is stranded with nothing merged.

4 occurrences in mcp-logs-parrot-sdd-coder: 2026-10-22T00:00:56Z, 2026-10-27 02:52:20Z / 12:01:06Z / 12:06:25Z. The last three are FEAT-753 TASK-4780 on the `glm` seat; two died at T+197s and T+198s after `coder_run_chunk`.

## Ruled out

No OOM (journalctl -k, 34 GiB free); no crash (coredumpctl empty, core_pattern wired to systemd-coredump); no `.so` rebuilt today; no host SIGINT (Claude logs that); no Python traceback on stderr.

## Root cause

`StdioMCPServer.start()` (mcp/local_server.py:87-89) ends the serve loop on stdin EOF (`if not line: break`) and exits 0 silently.

Claude Code hands the server **socketpairs**, not pipes (`/proc/<pid>/fd/0 -> socket:[...]`). `LLMCodeDispatcher._run_argv` (dispatchers/llm.py:2214) spawns the coder model's `run_command` children with `stdin=PIPE if stdin is not None else None` — i.e. **inherited** fd 0 in the normal case. `shutdown()` is socket-level, not fd-level, so an inheriting descendant that shuts stdin down EOFs the *server's* read.

Reproduced minimally: inherit+shutdown -> EOF (server exits); inherit+noop, DEVNULL+shutdown, DEVNULL+noop -> healthy.

Same class as the Codex hotfix `sdd/specs/codex-dispatch-stdin-isolation.spec.md` (codex.py:579 got DEVNULL); llm.py was not covered.

## Affected spawn sites (no `stdin=` -> inherit)

dispatchers/llm.py:2214, dispatchers/google_coding.py:407, sdd_coder/background.py:668, sdd_coder/background.py:1010. Clean: codex.py:579, procs.py:124.

Seats: nova / google-compat / zai / grok subclass LLMCodeDispatcher, so glm, minimax, qwen, mistral, gemini are exposed. codex and native seats are not.

## Secondary

Neither silent-exit path logs: the EOF `break` (local_server.py:89) and the SIGTERM handler's `os._exit(0)` (mcp/local_cli.py:80). That is why 4 failures left no trace.

## Fix

`stdin=DEVNULL` at the four sites; a log line before each silent exit; a regression test asserting every dev_loop spawn site isolates stdin.

## Workaround

Route affected tasks to a codex or native seat.

payload.title: Validate Code Search candidates at the requested ref before selecting SDD criteria
payload.body: Spec lines 278-279 accept a single default-branch Code Search hit directly. A hit can merely mention FEAT-759 inside another spec, or point to a path renamed/changed on base_ref. No header validation or fallback after a stale candidate is required. This can review against unrelated criteria or miss an existing base-branch spec. Require .spec.md path and exact Feature ID validation at the target ref, then directory fallback on invalid/missing candidates. Cover incidental mentions and renamed paths.

payload.title: Preserve Jira precedence when fetching a referenced ticket fails
payload.body: Spec lines 337-346 gate SDD fallback on ticket is None, although Goals require no fallback whenever a Jira key exists. _fetch_ticket returns None on missing toolkit, errors and missing issues (github_reviewer.py:1726-1749). A PR containing NAV and FEAT can thus receive an SDD approval during Jira failure instead of ticket_not_found. Gate fallback on absence of ticket_key and test Jira fetch failure in both entry points.

payload.title: Greedy prefix grammar consumes existing ADR/RFC citations
payload.body: Spec lines 246-248 and 321-323: proposed optional prefix consumes ADR1 in ADR1-ADR-2. Old GraphIndex emits ADR-1 and ADR-2; proposed grammar emits only ADR-2 even with no allowlist. ADR1-RFC-2 gives a wiki ADR match but no GraphIndex ADR match. Violates AC11 and lexical parity. Preserve existing token boundaries and add adjacent compact references to the regression corpus.

payload.title: Unlisted-prefix degradation contradicts missing-reference contract
payload.body: Spec lines 123-130 and AC8 require missing prefixed references not to resolve as bare references, but lines 255-262 discard unlisted prefixes even with a configured allowlist. With known FS, XX-ADR-3 normalizes to ADR-3 and resolves an existing bare record, or FS-ADR-3 via local fallback. Resolve the contract explicitly: scope AC8 to recognized prefixes and document unlisted behavior, or retain prefix provenance and define rejection for configured repositories.

payload.title: Prefixed filename grammar changes unconfigured ADR identities
payload.body: Spec lines 250-253 recognize fs-0042-use-pgvector.md where the old filename matcher returned no alias. Applying unlisted-prefix degradation adds ADR-42 without configuration. This changes external_id and citation links, or introduces a conflicting identifiers diagnostic with id ADR-7, violating line 440 full-sync compatibility. Gate new prefixed filename recognition on allowlist membership and add an unconfigured regression test.

payload.title: Local fallback must preserve ambiguous-reference diagnostics
payload.body: Spec lines 380-387 define lookup using only alias_map and local_prefix. The map has already dropped ambiguous aliases. A bare ADR-7 referring to two FS-ADR-7 records with local_prefix FS passes the current original-alias ambiguity check but the fallback returns None and is reported missing. Specify ambiguity handling for both exact and fallback candidates and test it; retain fail-closed behavior for ambiguous exact aliases.

payload.title: select_tests junit reporter overwrites test source files when outputFile is empty
payload.body: In scripts/sdd/select_tests.py the feature-tier vitest suite is invoked as `pnpm exec vitest run --reporter=junit --outputFile= <files>`. With an empty --outputFile, vitest writes the JUnit XML to the first test file path itself, overwriting src/lib/components/agents/canvas/a2ui/A2UIMermaidDiagram.test.ts with XML (observed on FEAT-753, 2026-10-27). The run then exits 1 with no baseline verdict. Fix: pass a real output path (e.g. under artifacts/logs/) or drop the junit reporter and parse the default output. Discovered while closing FEAT-753; test file restored from HEAD.
